newsitem.title: FRANCE: France against Turkish buffer zone in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: France against Turkish buffer zone in Iraq.

text.p: France said on Friday it opposed plans by Turkey to set up a buffer zone in northern Iraq which Washington said earlier it found acceptable.

"The international community has reaffirmed its commitment to Iraq's sovereignty and territorial integrity. That is valid now and in all circumstances," said Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt when questioned about Ankara's intentions.

Turkey has started a military build-up along its border with Kurdish-held northern Iraq ahead of creating a security zone up to 10 km (six miles) deep inside Iraq to check attacks by its own rebel Kurds.
Washington said on Wednesday it would not object if Ankara went ahead with the scheme.

French diplomats told reporters such a move would violate United Nations Security Council resolutions and Paris opposed a trend toward unilateral imposition of such buffer zones in international relations.

France, a Washington ally in the 1991 Gulf War, has differed with the United States over its cruise missle attacks against Iraq this week to punish President Saddam Hussein for sending troops into Kurdish areas in northern Iraq.

France said during a visit to Paris by U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher on Thursday that it would rejoin allied air patrols over Iraq but would not help patrol a U.S.-extended no-fly zone declared by President Bill Clinton in southern Iraq.
